title: Is ShipBob Different From a Traditional 3PL? What “More Than a 3PL” Means Day to Day
summary: Worried ShipBob is just a big, standardized 3PL? See what "more than a 3PL" means day to day, from complex requests to the control and support you keep.
body_markdown:
Merchants comparing fulfillment partners sometimes run into a specific worry about ShipBob: that it has grown into a big, standardized provider where the service turns cookie-cutter, unusual requests hit a wall, and you get less say over how your orders are handled than you would with a smaller, more hands-on shop.


It’s a fair thing to check. ShipBob describes itself as more than a traditional 3PL, and any time a company runs a large, consistent operation, it’s reasonable to ask whether “consistent” actually means “rigid,” and whether smaller accounts get lost inside the machine.


Perceptions vary for a few reasons. Some brands are comparing ShipBob to a small, local warehouse where they knew most people by name. Others are reading older reviews from a self-service era ShipBob has since moved past. And a lot of the summaries floating around describe the category in general, not how any one provider actually runs.


This guide breaks down where these worries come from, what “more than a 3PL” actually means once you’re a customer, and where a traditional provider stops versus where ShipBob keeps going, day to day.


## What merchants mean by “just another big 3PL”


A traditional[third-party logistics](https://www.shipbob.com/3pl/) (3PL) provider stores your inventory and ships your orders.


The concern here is that once a provider gets big enough, the very thing that makes it efficient, standardization, starts working against you.


Most versions of this concern rest on a few assumptions:


- A large, standardized provider delivers cookie-cutter service that feels impersonal, especially when something goes wrong.
- Standardized processes can’t absorb complex or unusual requests, like custom kitting or assembly, so those requests stall.
- A full-service model means you hand over control and lose visibility into how individual warehouse tasks get done.
- A smaller brand becomes a low-priority account inside a big operation, and attention is the first thing to go.


These are reasonable concerns, and they describe how some providers actually operate.


Here’s how the full-service model works at ShipBob, and why many brands experience the opposite.


## What “more than a 3PL” actually means


Let’s start with the short version.


A traditional 3PL rents you warehouse space and ships what’s in it.


A full-service model goes further: it standardizes the operation so the basics are reliable everywhere, then layers on the services, controls, and people a warehouse-that-only-ships doesn’t provide.


Standardization is the foundation that makes flexibility safe to offer. Because every location runs the same way, ShipBob can add custom work, overrides, and new regions on top without the operation breaking underneath.


That standard is also what keeps your experience consistent. Every ShipBob fulfillment center runs on the same proprietary[ShipBob WMS](https://www.shipbob.com/product/wms/) and the same service standards, so you get the same experience whichever fulfillment center ships your order, one location or several across countries.


💡


Check out ShipBob’s approach to[consistent, accurate fulfillment](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/shipbob-accurate-fulfillment/) for more details on this.


One reason a standardized model can still flex is that ShipBob owns the technology it runs on. The warehouse management system, the routing logic, and the merchant dashboard were built in-house for this network, so when a workflow needs to change, there’s no third-party vendor to wait on.


## Where a traditional 3PL stops and where ShipBob keeps going


None of this shows up on a spec sheet. You notice it once you’re running on the platform, in the moments a traditional provider would hand the problem back to you.


### 1. Complex and custom requests run inside the model, not around it


One common worry is that unusual requests, like custom kitting, break a standardized system. In a full-service model, that work is a built-in service.


**What this actually means:**


Custom packaging, bundles, gift sets, inserts, and other[value-added services like kitting](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/kitting/) are configured and run inside ShipBob’s fulfillment centers through the[Customization Suite](https://www.shipbob.com/product/customization-suite/) , with published turnaround times.


When a setup doesn’t fit a standard configuration, ShipBob’s Solutions Architecture team builds the integration or workflow around your business instead of forcing you into the default.


**Why it matters:**


- Complexity scales without turning into a fire drill for your team.
- The same custom experience ships every time, even when volume spikes.
- You add capabilities like kitting or branded packaging as you grow, without switching providers.


**Proof** : When[Our Place](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/our-place/) needed its own custom packaging instead of standard boxes, ShipBob built those boxes into its packing algorithm so every parcel still shipped in the right-sized box.


Our Place runs fulfillment across six fulfillment centers with a two-person operations team, and after expanding from two US warehouses to four, the brand cut delivery times from five or six days down to two and a half and saved roughly $1.5 million in freight costs.


> *“We sought a fulfillment partner primarily for their exceptional operational capabilities. Our priority was finding a partner capable of efficiently handling large-scale fulfillment while also streamlining our workflows.*
>
>
> *ShipBob emerged as the perfect fit, meeting our needs beyond expectation. Our Operations team operates with remarkable efficiency, often assigning a single talented individual to manage all workflows within an entire function.*
>
>
> *A prime illustration is our fulfillment department, where one individual oversees end-to-end operations across seven warehouses. This level of accountability for a mid-market brand is made possible by ShipBob’s technology and extensive network, which handles a significant portion of the operational workload. Consequently, we can direct our attention towards managing exceptions within workflows instead of the workflow itself.”*
>
>
> Ali Shahid, COO of Our Place


Our Place


### 2. You still set the rules and keep the controls


The next worry, that a full-service model means giving up granular control, gets the relationship backwards. Full-service means ShipBob runs the day-to-day operation, not that you lose the switches.


**What this actually means:**


- You set the order rules that decide how orders are handled.
- You can override how the[Inventory Placement Program (IPP)](https://www.shipbob.com/product/inventory-placement/) distributes your inventory when you’d rather allocate it differently.
- You can turn off a carrier you don’t want to use.
- You define what happens to returns, whether items are restocked, quarantined, or disposed of.


Automation runs the default so your team isn’t touching every order by hand, and the override stays with you.


**Why it matters:**


- Control over the details that matter to your brand, without the manual work.
- Automation for the routine, with the final say still yours.
- No forced trade-off between running lean and staying in control.


**Proof** :[Aroma360](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/aroma360/) built its brand on the unboxing experience and wanted its fulfillment partner to run like its marketing stack. In ShipBob’s Rules Engine, the team creates a rule and tagging system to manage which orders receive custom marketing inserts, and the same logic handles custom packaging, like sending a specific candle out in a specific bag. The result is a level of control Aroma360 had never seen from a partner, with rules it can change on the fly as its business changes.


> *“We really focus on the unboxing and post-purchase experience, so ShipBob’s robust customization capabilities make it so easy for us to add special touches like marketing inserts to an order.*
>
>
> *We were just recently running a bunch of different inserts and were able to handle the majority of that on our end via ShipBob’s tagging rules. All I have to do is go into ShipBob’s Rules Engine, and create a rule that says, “If an order has this tag, add an insert.” I’ve never seen that before where our fulfillment partner can operate similar to how we run marketing email campaigns with tags and rules.*
>
>
> *We also use ShipBob’s Rule Engine to implement custom packaging elements, like custom dividers and bubble wrap. I’ll create a rule on my end where every time a certain candle comes on an order, ShipBob knows to put the ordered items in a specific bag. It’s all quick and easy, and we can aways change rules on the fly as our business changes.”*
>
>
> Rachel Tannenholz, President, and Melissa Mosheim, Director of Logistics at Aroma360


### 3. There’s a people layer a warehouse-that-ships doesn’t offer


The last worry, that a smaller account disappears inside a big operation, is really a question about people. A traditional 3PL gives you a warehouse. A full-service partner gives you a team.


**What this actually means:**


- Qualified accounts get a dedicated Merchant Success Manager who learns your business and runs regular reviews.
- On-site representatives work the floor of the fulfillment centers for direct warehouse communication.
- Merchant Care is staffed by full-time ShipBob employees, not an outsourced call center, with direct access to your account history.
- When an issue is technical, it goes to a specialized team rather than bouncing between generalists, and when a standard setup doesn’t fit, the Solutions Architecture team steps in.


ShipBob’s guide to[personal, responsive support](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/shipbob-customer-support/) covers this side in more detail.


**Why it matters:**


- More support structure as you grow, not less.
- Accountability with a name attached, instead of a ticket queue.
- Direct lines to the warehouse floor and to technical help when you need them.


**Proof** :[CRIMPiT](https://www.shipbob.com/blog/crimpit/) moved from packing orders in its own warehouse to running six ShipBob fulfillment centers across three countries, standardizing its process across all of them without losing the hands-on relationship. “With ShipBob we’ve been able to create a standardized model for the UK, Europe, and North America,” said co-founder Michael Harper, and that consistency came alongside, not instead of, a close support relationship.


Outsourcing this way freed up the equivalent of 112 hours a week the founders had been pouring into fulfillment.


> *“One of the best parts of working with ShipBob is our account manager. She’s probably the best account manager we’ve ever experienced with a business. She goes to bat for us and is a strong advocate for CRIMPiT. We’ll ask her if they’re available to jump on a call and within 20 minutes we’re talking on the phone to resolve any questions we have. Also, since we’re within the UK and an hour from the fulfillment center, if we ever need to be face-to-face, we can easily do that. There are a lot of benefits to working with ShipBob’s team.”*
>
>
> Michael Harper, Co-Founder of CRIMPiT, and Sean Togher, Finance Director at CRIMPiT


## What to expect from ShipBob day to day


A traditional 3PL stores your products and ships them. A full-service model does that and keeps going: one standard across every fulfillment center so your experience stays consistent, custom work handled as a service, the controls left in your hands, and a team you can actually reach. That’s what “more than a 3PL” means once the contract is signed.


If you’re comparing partners, it’s worth asking each one exactly where their service stops. Connect with our team to see what a full-service model would look like for your brand.


[Speak with a Fulfillment Expert](https://www.shipbob.com/quote/)


## FAQs about working with ShipBob versus a traditional 3PL


#### Is ShipBob a 3PL?


ShipBob is more than a traditional 3PL. It does everything a traditional third-party logistics provider does, including storage, picking, packing, and shipping, and is built to go further as a full-service fulfillment platform. But alongside core fulfillment, ShipBob adds owned technology, value-added services, and a dedicated support team, which is why it’s described as more than a traditional 3PL.


#### What’s different about working with ShipBob versus a traditional 3PL?


A traditional 3PL rents you space and ships what’s in it. ShipBob standardizes fulfillment across its network, handles custom requests as built-in services, and gives you controls and a support team on top, so consistency and flexibility come from the same partner.


#### Do I lose control when I outsource to a large provider?


No. With ShipBob, you set the order rules, can override inventory placement, choose or disable carriers, and define how returns are handled. Automation runs the routine work while the decisions stay with you.


#### Can ShipBob handle complex or custom requirements?


Yes. Custom packaging, kitting, bundles, and inserts run inside ShipBob’s fulfillment centers through the Customization Suite, and the Solutions Architecture team builds custom integrations or workflows when a standard setup doesn’t fit.


#### Who do I actually deal with day to day?


Day to day, you work with ShipBob’s Merchant Care team of full-time employees, plus on-site representatives in the fulfillment centers. Qualified accounts also get a dedicated Merchant Success Manager who knows your business and runs regular reviews.
